title: Confined-demand beta decay and confinement universality
html:
Beta decay emerges from the confined deficit

The \mathcal{B}_3-confined proton NF has residual deficit:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{p})
  =
  \underbrace{-0.100}_{\gamma < 0}\gamma + 0.036\sigma_0 + 0.998\sigma_1 + 0.099 L_+ + 0.009 L_- + \underbrace{-0.043}_{e^- < 0}e^-.
  • \gamma < 0: vacuum energy deficit—the source of the nucleon's mass.
  • e^- < 0: trefoil deficit—the nucleon possesses a topological deficit corresponding to an electron. This is the categorical beta decay channel.

For the neutron, the deficit is larger: \gamma = -0.202, L_+ = -0.010, e^- = -0.044. The additional L_+ deficit and larger \gamma deficit provide the energy that drives \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar\nu.

Confinement universality

The confined nucleon NF depends only on q_0 and the quark types. It is independent of the photon polarization (\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) that created the quarks. The strong interaction washes out the electromagnetic initial conditions.
